definitions.explanation: A standardized application form used in Japanese job hunting. Companies require applicants to fill out an entry sheet as the first step in the hiring process, typically including self-introduction, motivation, and strengths.

notes:
A wasei-eigo (Japanese-coined English) term abbreviated as ES. Central to the ⟦{就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}→就職活動：14840_shuushokukatsudou⟧ (job-hunting) process in Japan, where university students apply to multiple companies simultaneously. Unlike a Western-style resume, the entry sheet is a company-specific form with essay-style questions.

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese ⟦{新卒|しんそつ}{採用|さいよう}→新卒採用：29208_shinsotsusaiyou⟧ (new graduate hiring), the entry sheet is the first hurdle. Thousands of students may apply to a single company, and many are screened out at this stage. Students often attend ⟦{就活|しゅうかつ}→就活：05832_shuukatsu⟧⟦セミナー→セミナー：11000_seminaa⟧ to learn how to write effective entry sheets.
